Google storage for me was just the worst in every way.
I tried to download my cloud photos from my old iPhone so I could have them locally downloaded. There was no way to mass download them so I had to do this manually for nearly 400 photos.
If that was the end of it I would have been fine, but I had to do this two more times because I think Google was detecting that I already had the photos through the cloud and deleting my downloaded ones.
I'm not 100% sure if it was Google doing this, because Google never gave any notification nor did it ask permission, but it stopped after I disabled the app and I haven't had issues since.

I also got tired of Google constantly asking me to backup my photos and then making the menu take more than 1 tap to go away. I already disapprove of *all* unwarranted popups, but for every button press it takes to make them go away they get exponentially more annoying. If I wanted to back up my photos, I would ask.

Then there was Google telling me I should delete a bunch of my photos to save storage(my storage is nowhere near full) while Google photos was using half a gigabyte just in cache storage, which was only marginally less than what deleting the photos would have saved.

text:
Seems that the lock folder is actually a locked CLOUD folder. You Must be connected to the internet with the phone in order to use it. 

If at any time you delete the app, you also will lose the Cloud folder along with every photo you have given to Google. It will still be on their servers, but you will not have access to it. 

The lock folder is in NO WAY a hidden folder!!

The only person you are hiding the pictures from is yourself. And that is only because of the screwy location inside the app to find the Cloud folder.

If someone has password/fingerprint access to your phone, they too will have access to all of your locked photos if they take the time to look inside the app. And Google itself won't need to access your phone since you're uploading the photos to them directly.

text: Good plan Neil, but with one small catch! When you set up a new account and tell it to backup your photos, it will backup ALL the photos that are stored on your phone, not just the most recent year, which could mean several year's worth, so you'll be in the same position you were when you started. If you want an account for each year, for example, you'd need to make sure your phone ONLY had this year's photos on it. Then you'd need to delete them all from your phone before starting a new account for the next year. Also beware some services sync rather than backup, which means when you delete on your phone, it deletes them online too. The moral being to always backup photos onto a separate physical drive somewhere before doing anything clever!

If you want an account for each year, for example, you'd need to make sure your phone ONLY had this year's photos on it. Then you'd need to delete them all from your phone before starting a new account for the next year. Also beware some services sync rather than backup, which means when you delete on your phone, it deletes them online too. The moral being to always backup photos onto a separate physical drive somewhere before doing anything clever!

How I Used ChatGPT to Write This Essay 💀
So basically, I had to write an essay.
And instead of actually writing the essay myself like a normal human being, I opened ChatGPT.
I typed:
“Write a long long essay about how I used ChatGPT to create this essay.”
And bro actually did it.
Like... I literally asked ChatGPT to write an essay about me using ChatGPT to write the essay.
This is not a story.
This is not some made-up scenario.
This is literally happening right now.
I am using ChatGPT to write this exact essay.
And somehow, I'm still calling it my essay 💀
My contribution was basically opening the app and typing the prompt.
ChatGPT's contribution?
The entire essay.
Absolute generational teamwork.
I could've spent an hour sitting there staring at a blank Google Doc like:
“Hmm... what should I write?”
Instead, I said:
“ChatGPT, lock in.”
And ChatGPT locked in harder than I ever could.
The funniest part is that I am literally making ChatGPT explain how I used ChatGPT.
So ChatGPT is basically writing its own behind-the-scenes documentary.
Bro is the writer AND the subject 😭
And then I realized I needed the essay to be long.
So obviously, I told ChatGPT to make it long.
Because apparently the secret to getting a good grade is just having enough words to make your teacher scroll for 14 minutes.
If one paragraph isn't enough, add another.
If another paragraph isn't enough, add another.
And if the essay is STILL not long enough...
“ChatGPT, make it longer.”
Boom.
Another 700 words appeared.
At this point, I'm not even writing.
I'm just giving commands.
I'm basically the CEO of an AI-powered writing company where the only employee is ChatGPT and I'm doing absolutely nothing 💀.
But honestly, this is kinda insane.
A few years ago, if someone told me I'd be able to tell an AI what I wanted to write and have it generate the whole thing almost instantly, I'd probably think they were talking about some futuristic movie.
Now I'm literally doing it for a YouTube video.
And I'm not even trying to hide it.
I'm openly admitting that ChatGPT wrote this.
There is no plot twist.
There is no “and then I realized the AI had secretly written the essay.”
NO.
I KNEW.
I ASKED IT TO.
That is the whole joke.
The entire essay is basically:
“I used ChatGPT.”
“ChatGPT wrote it.”
“Look, ChatGPT is writing about ChatGPT writing it.”
“Anyway, here's another paragraph.”
And somehow we're still here.
Honestly, I could probably ask ChatGPT to write an essay about this essay, then ask it to write an essay about the essay about this essay.
Then we'd have an essay so confusing that even ChatGPT would be like:
“Bro what are you doing 😭”
But that's future me's problem.
For now, the mission is simple.
I needed an essay.
I used ChatGPT.
ChatGPT wrote the essay.
I am now explaining that ChatGPT wrote the essay.
And you're reading the explanation.
So technically...
ChatGPT wrote this.
I just had the idea.
Big difference.
I am not lazy.
I am simply AI-assisted.
That's what we're calling it.
And if anyone asks how long it took me to write this essay, I'm just going to say:
“Not long.”
Because technically...
I didn't write it.
I prompted it.
Huge difference.
Anyway, thanks for watching this extremely unnecessary essay about me using ChatGPT to write this extremely unnecessary essay.
If you made it this far, you're actually a legend.
And ChatGPT...
You cooked.
I think.
Maybe.
I don't know.
I'm just the guy who typed the prompt. 💀

A crítica não é para desmerecer a tecnologia, muito pelo contrário. O ChatGPT evoluiu muito, mas justamente por isso o recurso de voz também merece uma atenção maior. Quem paga espera qualidade, estabilidade e uma experiência realmente fluida.
Seria muito bom ver a equipe responsável priorizando esses problemas e trabalhando para reduzir significativamente essas falhas. Porque, sinceramente, pagar caro por um recurso que ainda gagueja, apresenta ruídos e sofre com gargalos acaba gerando uma sensação de que estamos pagando hoje por uma experiência que só ficará realmente boa daqui a muitos anos. 😂

❤❤ Meanwhile, ChatGPT’s voice feature continues to experience issues that significantly affect the overall experience: stuttering, bottlenecks, crackling, background noise, audio cuts, and a general lack of fluency.

It’s difficult not to feel frustrated when you pay a considerable amount for a tool that is supposed to provide a more stable and natural voice experience. For paid plans, the expectation is precisely to have access to more advanced features with higher quality — not to encounter a voice feature that still suffers from so many technical problems.

This criticism is not meant to discredit the technology. Quite the opposite. ChatGPT has evolved tremendously, and precisely because of that, the voice feature also deserves greater attention. People who pay expect quality, stability, and an experience that truly feels smooth and natural.

It would be great to see the team responsible for the voice experience prioritize these issues and work on significantly reducing these problems. Because, honestly, paying a high price for a feature that still stutters, produces noise, and suffers from audio bottlenecks can leave users with the feeling that we are paying today for an experience that may only become truly good many years from now. 😂

text: Suggestion:  before backing up/uploading to GPhotos, organize them into folder/s on your PC by event, or subject, or item.  Windows has excellent Batch Processing functionality.  Once in File Explorer, locate your folder.  Be sure to click "View" tab where you will then see "Panes" and also "Layout" sections at top.  Both should be set to "Details."  Then rename the folder to whatever: "1970 Jones Family Vacation" or "Jones 1970 Family Vacation."  Then highlight all the related photos within it (do NOT include videos).  Right click & rename one, using same name as folder. They will all be named the same with a sequential (#) following.  Then, while all are highlighted, edit the detailed metadata shown in the far right column with whatever...Date Taken, Location, Comments, Title, Tags, etc.  After batch processing your event photos, THEN upload to Google Photos and the basic, important metadata, including date, will stay with each photo, and sort by date.

text: Good job on this video. I inherited old printed photos going back into the late 1800's (mostly family prints of ancestors),  photos taken in my early years from the 40's on, slides of vacation trips in my childhood, etc. I realized that my descendants would not have any interest in any of these unless the pictures included identified ancestors. Pictures of parks, buildings, etc. would never be viewed by anyone. So, my first task was to identify people in the photos, then discard all printed photos and slides that had no known descendants or close friends. Then, I sorted the remaining pictures by surname, year, or event, and scanned them (using an Epson scanner) into digital folders. Each picture was titled with the year/names/location if known. I then uploaded these into Google Drive, shared them with relatives, and saved the originals on my PC. Google Photos grabbed these as well, but the organized folders were of course not retained.

Me sorprende mucho como todavía seguimos picando en los trucos de marketing de Apple. 
Es decir, nos dicen que la ventaja sobre Google es porque “es más privado”. Y es más privado porque el “análisis de nuestras fotos se hace en el dispositivo y no en la nube”. Nosotros decimos “hostia! Es verdad que privado que es” pero no nos paramos a analizar si tiene algún sentido lo que dicen o en qué mejora exactamente la privacidad el hecho de que el análisis se haga en local, cuando las fotos (que es aquello que queremos proteger), esta subido a la nube igual. Por no decir que los metadatos fruto de ese análisis se suben a la nube igual porque si no luego no estarían accesibles desde nuestro Mac o nuestro iPad.
iCloud no es ni mas ni menos seguro que Google Fotos, pero sin duda es menos completo, y Apple suple sus carencias con afirmaciones abstractas de dudosa base técnica, jugando con el desconocimiento y fe de sus usurarios,  para darle un valor añadido artificial. I think your advice is a bit dated. 
1) Since most people now days use laptops with limited space it is not practical to gather all photos (and videos) in the internal drive. Space will lbe a limiting factor.
2) For larger collections of media I strongly recommend using an app like Lightroom. With most of these apps you can easily find photos based on date regardless of where and how they are physically stored.
3) In apps like Lightroom you can create collections or virtual folder for easy access to images with a common theme. The same photo can be maid available in multiple collections without actually create physical copies.
The most important part of some organisation of media on drives (internally or externally) is to simplify the important task of making backups.

I use a command line program called XXCOPY.

This searches the various hard drives for pictures. Moves them onto whatever drive is needed.

Xxcopy F:\*.JPG C:\NEWFOLDER\/S /CCY

This will go to the F:
Will look for anything ending in .JPG  then the /S wil keep the folder tree the same in the copy as the original.  /CCY   means copy
